title: Auxiliary equivariant cover with no rational fibre curves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and $f:P\to S$ an H-projective morphism with $P$ integral of finite type over $k$. Suppose every geometric fibre of $f$ is pure of dimension one and its generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral. Let $M\subset P$ be a closed subset whose reduced generic fibre is finite etale. Let a finite group $H$ act compatibly on $k,P,S,f$, preserving $M$. Write $K=k(S)$ and $F=k(P)$. There are a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $S_1$, a finite surjective morphism $S_1\to S$ with finite separable function-field extension $K_1/K$, an integral finite-type $k$-scheme $Q$, a finite surjective morphism $Q\to P\times_S S_1$, and a finite group $H_1$ with a surjection $\beta:H_1\to H$ acting compatibly on this diagram and on $k$. The morphism $Q\to S_1$ is H-projective, with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres. Its generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral. Every irreducible component of every geometric fibre has normalization of genus at least two; in particular every morphism from $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ to such a fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is constant. The reduced inverse image of $M$ in the generic fibre of $Q$ is a finite set of distinct $K_1$-rational points, stable as a set under $H_1$. The extensions $k(Q)/F$ and $K_1/K$ are finite separable. For $A_1=\ker\beta$, the embeddings from the diagram identify $k(Q)^{A_1}=F$ and $K_1^{A_1}=K$. No semistability, nodal reduction, flatness of $Q\to S_1$, or extension of the generic markings as disjoint sections over $S_1$ is asserted.

The notions of field, integral scheme, proper morphism, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, projectivity, finite morphism, surjectivity, function field and field extension use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes that is finite over a dense open of its target. Group actions may be nonfaithful and may act on the ground field. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions, fibre products and etaleness use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normalization, completion and power series use [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; the genus of a smooth projective geometrically integral curve is [def-pc-genus].

proof.text: Choose a prime $\ell\geq5$ different from $\operatorname{char}k$ (one of $5,7$). Apply equivariant pencil preparation to the reduced generic marking. Obtain $K_0,H_0,A_0,S_0,P_0,F_0$, the pencils $x_i$, and $K_0^{A_0}=K$, $F_0^{A_0}=F$. This includes the zero-dimensional base case.

Apply the orbit-Kummer model lemma to these pencils and the $H_0$-stable marking. It gives $L,E,J,N,Q_1/T$, with $J\twoheadrightarrow H_0$, $L^N=F_0$, $E^N=K_0$, and reduced generic marking finite etale over $E$. The identity translates supply the two $\ell$th roots for each pencil. Fermat domination gives genus at least two for every normalized geometric component of $Q_1/T$.

Rationalize this generic marking by the equivariant marking lemma. Write its output as $K_2,H_2,N_2,Q_2/S_2$, so $H_2\twoheadrightarrow J$, $L_2=L\otimes_EK_2$, $L_2^{N_2}=L$ and $K_2^{N_2}=E$. Its generic marking is a stable set of distinct $K_2$-rational points, and all normalized geometric components retain genus at least two. The general projective-line clause of the Fermat-domination lemma now makes every $\mathbf P^1_\Omega\to(Q_2)_s$ constant.

Put $A'=\ker(J\to H)$ and $A_2=\ker(H_2\to H)$. The map $A'\to A_0$ is onto with kernel $N$, and $A_2\to A'$ is onto with kernel $N_2$. An $A'$-fixed element of $L$ first belongs to $L^N=F_0$ and is then $A_0$-fixed, so $L^{A'}=F$; conversely every element of $F$ is fixed. On constants $E^{A'}=K$. Repeating this argument gives $L_2^{A_2}=F$ and $K_2^{A_2}=K$, with the embeddings of the diagram.

The three model maps are finite surjective onto the full base changes. Base change $P_0\to P\times_SS_0$ and $Q_1\to P_0\times_{S_0}T$ to $S_2$, and compose with $Q_2\to Q_1\times_TS_2$. Finiteness is preserved by base change and composition; affine-locally surjectivity survives base change by the spectrum lemma, and surjections compose. Thus $Q_2\to P\times_SS_2$ is finite surjective. All constant, radical and scalar field extensions are finite separable by the three construction lemmas; transitivity gives $L_2/F$ and $K_2/K$ finite separable. Their models give projectivity, finite type, pure curve fibres and the smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. Rename $(S_2,Q_2,K_2,H_2)$ as $(S_1,Q,K_1,H_1)$ and take the composite group surjection as $\beta$.
